## Surgical Blades — Pattern and Clinical Use

Blade shape determines the incision. The No. 10 is the general-purpose belly blade for skin, the No. 11 is a straight pointed blade for stab incisions and drainage, the No. 12 is a curved hook used for suture removal and specific dissections, and the No. 15 is a small curved blade for short, precise incisions. Each batch passes Rockwell hardness testing, dimensional checks on edge consistency across lot, and visual inspection under our ISO 13485 system before passivation and final finishing. Mirror and satin finishes are both available — satin is usually specified where glare under operating lights is a concern.

## Who Sources Surgical Blades From Surgical Star

Blades are a recurring consumable, which makes them one of the strongest repeat-revenue lines in a catalog. They sell to hospital, dental, veterinary and podiatry distributors and pair directly with a handle range.

## OEM, Certification and Ordering

Every surgical blades can be produced as a private-label line: your logo laser-marked on the wrapper, your catalog numbers, and your own printed packaging, manufactured from your drawings or a reference sample.
